channels.name: SDA
channels.purpose: Serial Data Line. Carries address byte + data bytes + ACK/NACK bit. Open-drain, wired-AND: any device can pull LOW; HIGH is achieved by all devices releasing the line.
channels.active_levels: 0 = LOW (driven); 1 = HIGH-Z (released, pulled up by Rp to VDD)

channels.name: SCL
channels.direction_master: output (drives clock); also released to allow slave clock-stretching
channels.direction_slave: input (samples on rising edge); optional output (pulls LOW to stretch)
channels.purpose: Serial Clock Line. Master drives clock pulses; slave may pull LOW to stretch. 9 pulses per byte (8 data + 1 ACK).
channels.active_levels: 0 = LOW (driven by master, or stretched by slave); 1 = HIGH-Z (released, pulled up by Rp)

ufm_channels.name: USDA
ufm_channels.purpose: Ultra Fast-mode serial data. Push-pull, unidirectional (master-to-slave only). No ACK; the 9th SCL pulse drives SDA HIGH ignoring response.

ufm_channels.name: USCL
ufm_channels.purpose: Ultra Fast-mode serial clock. Push-pull, unidirectional. Master drives all clock pulses; no clock stretching.

global_signals.name: VDD
global_signals.purpose: Supply voltage. Determines VIL (0.3 VDD) and VIH (0.7 VDD) thresholds for non-legacy devices.

global_signals.name: Rp
global_signals.purpose: Pull-up resistor on SDA and SCL to VDD; sized per mode and bus capacitance.

global_signals.name: GND
global_signals.purpose: Common ground reference for all devices on the bus.

ordering_rules.byte_count: Number of bytes per transfer is unrestricted (limited only by master's STOP).
ordering_rules.ack_per_byte: Each byte (including address byte) is followed by exactly one ACK / NACK bit on the 9th SCL pulse.

dependency_graph.common_rule: Master drives SCL; slaves sample SDA on rising SCL. Data on SDA must be stable while SCL HIGH; only S/P/Sr violate this rule.
dependency_graph.data_dependency: Receiver's ACK on byte N permits transmitter to send byte N+1. Slave's clock-stretching on SCL forces master to wait.

handshake_pairs.name: ADDR_ACK
handshake_pairs.rule: After 8-bit address byte: slave pulls SDA LOW on 9th SCL pulse → addressed; HIGH → not addressed (NACK).

handshake_pairs.name: DATA_ACK
handshake_pairs.rule: After each 8-bit data byte: receiver pulls SDA LOW on 9th SCL pulse to ACK; HIGH = NACK.

handshake_pairs.name: CLOCK_STRETCH
handshake_pairs.rule: Slave holds SCL LOW after 8th pulse to delay next byte; master waits.

handshake_pairs.name: ARBITRATION
handshake_pairs.rule: On SDA while SCL HIGH: each master compares actual SDA to its driven value; mismatch = arbitration loss → release SDA.
